acquisition-viability.resolution: COMPLETE 2026-08-26 - THE SPRINT DEFINITION OF DONE, MET. Ben criterion: a corporation CAN save up over a few economy ticks to buy another company and still be making a profit afterwards. 7/8 seeds accumulate (mean +51 cr/qtr); all 5 seeds offering an above-zero-priced public firm reached its price in 1-25 quarters (mean 8.6, about two in-game years); the buy applied through the real buy_corporation verb; 5/5 still earning 20 quarters later with the acquired maintenance folded in. R4: rival solvency 79.7 to 73.7 percent, field holdings +39.4 percent, 3356 rival units standing - the gate did not go green by draining the field. R0 held: 42 of 47 resources priced, config parsed and passed, count printed. R5: k_acquisition_multiple LEFT AT 8.0 with three reasons measured rather than asserted - the profit term is 7.4 percent of the price magnitude and NEGATIVE, so raising it makes a bad firm cheaper, and on the cheapest-firm gate the floor decides the price at any multiple. CAVEAT ON THE RECORD: 3 of 8 seeds offered no above-zero-priced public firm at all, and the one seed whose seat missed the viability floor is the one that does not accumulate. The loop closes where the world offers a solvent public firm.

rows.evidence:
COMPLETE 2026-09-06. history_sim_state gains works_by_band / units_by_band / works_by_span / units_by_span, counted at the event. build_stack REPORTS the band it fielded via an out-param rather than the call site re-deriving min_band - a second copy would be free to drift. span_index() handles the INT64_MIN sentinel explicitly so a single-span ancient arc reports span 0, not an industrial span it does not have. history_sweep prints the per-band and per-span table and asserts B1. WORKS ARE ZERO IN EVERY BAND - that is BL-757 (build_work never wins the scored contest), reported not asserted past, exactly as the requirement directed.

CORRECTED 2026-09-06 AFTER THE COLD REVIEW BARRIER. THIS ROW WAS MARKED COMPLETE ON EVIDENCE THAT COULD NOT BEAR ON IT, and the review was right. TWO REAL DEFECTS. (1) The counters were two 1-D MARGINALS (units_by_band and units_by_span), which cannot answer a cross-tabulated question: a medieval span-1 ceiling fielding gunpowder in span 1 produces marginals IDENTICAL to an unrestricted run fielding gunpowder in span 0. The counter built to see the ceiling was blind to the case it existed for. NOW A TRUE CROSS-TAB, [span][band]. (2) THE VERIFYING RUN HAD NO BOUNDARY: history_sweep was run without --epoch, so boundary_year was INT64_MIN and "either side of the boundary" was never exercised - the 32a lesson repeating in the same sprint. RE-RUN with --epoch 1960, which has a real 1560 boundary: span 0 classical 3,988,542 / medieval 21,633; span 1 classical 5,245,315 / medieval 1,500; gunpowder and industrial zero in both. B1 now gates on an industrial span being PRESENT, because on a single-span arc sim_band_ceiling is unrestricted and asserting a ceiling there would assert a property the sim does not enforce. HONEST LIMIT: no polity reaches gunpowder even UNRESTRICTED in these seeds, so the observable now exists and is correct, but the ceiling has still never been seen BINDING.

rows.requirement: `run_continents` returns an ordered sequence of plate snapshots with a DEFINED epoch length. `drift_col`/`drift_row` are integrated by an explicit loop rather than documented as "per-epoch" with no epoch defined anywhere.
verification: headless: a harness asserts the sequence is ordered, non-empty, and its epoch length is a stated parameter
rows.notes: The row asked for a returned sequence. A derived one is strictly better here because of the save seam, and the reasoning is in the header comment beside the constants so the next reader does not re-litigate it.
rows.evidence: COMPLETE 2026-09-03, with a deliberate deviation stated rather than smuggled. The epoch length and depth are now STATED constants - continent_epoch_years = 5,000,000 (one grid column is ~153 km and Earth-like plate motion covers that in 3-6 My, so the clamped 0.15-1.2 columns per epoch sits at a plausible rate) and continent_drift_epochs = 20, which is 100 My. continent_snapshot_at(cs, e, gw, gh) reconstructs any epoch. THE DEVIATION: run_continents does NOT return a stored sequence. continent_state is on the save ENVELOPE seam, and 20 plate_id rasters at 31,581 tiles each is ~2.5 MB of save per body for data that is a pure function of five floats per plate. The sequence is therefore DERIVABLE - snapshot_at over [0, depth] - and costs nothing until asked for. continent_drift C2b asserts the age arithmetic.

rows.requirement: THE ENDPOINT IS UNCHANGED. The final snapshot is identical to today's `continent_state` output, so nothing downstream of continents moves and the 0 CE digests hold.
verification: headless: world_determinism - the three 2026-09-03 digests unchanged
rows.notes: The sequence is additive; the present-day answer must be bit-identical or the item has changed the world rather than described its past.
rows.evidence: COMPLETE 2026-09-03. world_determinism digests unmoved: 039EE9880739CDF6 / B0EBBA249B3DDABB / DE55600457797638, era report years=400 battles=270 conquests=207 foundings=833. And the sharper check is in the new harness rather than in the world: continent_drift C1 asserts that epoch 0 reproduces continent_state::plate_id BIT-IDENTICALLY, using the same comparison and the same strict-< tie-break as run_continents own Voronoi. That identity is what makes every deeper epoch a reconstruction instead of a fiction - if zero offset disagreed with the present, nothing built on this would mean anything.

rows.requirement: The shared plate RNG stream is not disturbed. `run_continents` draws every plate's position, direction and oceanic flag from one stream in a fixed order; any new draw inserted into that loop shifts every subsequent plate.
verification: static: review confirms no draw was inserted before an existing one
rows.evidence: COMPLETE 2026-09-03, and asserted rather than reasoned. The snapshot consumes NO randomness - it winds existing seeds back along drift vectors and re-runs the Voronoi - so no draw was inserted into the shared plate stream, which draws position, direction and oceanic flag for every plate in one fixed order. continent_drift C4 proves the stream is where it was: a second run_continents at the same seed produces identical plates AND identical plate_id.

rows.requirement: The expensive neighbour is NOT re-run per epoch. The rift-basin search (corridor_of, O(total) per candidate pair with a 25-sample inlandness probe per corridor tile) runs once, not once per snapshot.
verification: headless: the harness reports per-epoch wall clock, and total cost stays within single-digit ms per snapshot
rows.notes: Feasibility measured the Voronoi snapshot as cheap (~316k distance evals) and named the basin search as the real cost.
rows.evidence: COMPLETE 2026-09-03, reported not asserted. Measured by continent_drift C6: 21 snapshots in 5.1 ms, 0.24 ms each, against 2.8 ms for one full run_continents - so a snapshot is ~12x cheaper than the pass, which is the observable form of 'the rift-basin search is not re-run'. snapshot_at deliberately does neither the boundary classification nor the basin search: the basin search describes the PRESENT surface, so re-running it per epoch would cost more and mean less. CAVEAT ON THE COMPARISON: the harness builds its planetology_state by hand, so its run_continents baseline may not exercise every gate the real pass does - the ratio is indicative, not a budget.

rows.notes: BASELINE CORRECTED 2026-09-03. The note first read "world build 11.2 s with prehistory on vs 4.79 s off, so the 400-year era pass is 6.4 s". That was a MISREADING of the pre-change harness output: 6.45 s was the whole world build with prehistory on, not the era pass, and 11.2 s was never a figure the harness printed. The instrumentation this row added is what settles it.
rows.evidence:
COMPLETE 2026-09-03. Generation now reports per-pass wall clock and the span structure; world_determinism prints both. Measured on the merged tree, RELEASE harness path (build_lua_harness.bat -> build_gen/verify/), which memory io-headless-build-invocation names as the evidence path:

  0 CE, 400 y      total 8200 ms = pre-settlement 443 + settlement 4 + ERA-1 323 + post-era 7428
  0 CE, no era     total 6661 ms = pre-settlement 455 + settlement 3 + ERA-1   0 + post-era 6202
  1960, two-span   total 7996 ms = pre-settlement 465 + settlement 2 + ERA-1 197 + post-era 7331

TWO FINDINGS. (1) THE SECOND SPAN IS FREE, and in fact cheaper: 800 years at epoch 1960 costs 197 ms against 323 ms for 400 years at 0 CE. Cost tracks the region table the sim grows, not the years it walks, and at 1960 the settlement pass has already founded most regions - 506 sim foundings against 833. (2) THE ERA PASS COSTS 4x ITS OWN WALL CLOCK. Era on vs off at 0 CE is a ~1.5 s difference of which only 323 ms is the sim; the rest is the post-era passes working over the 833 regions it founded. Anyone budgeting the era off its own timer is wrong by four. Reported, never asserted.

BUILD TYPE IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT (cold review, 2026-09-03). The same passes in a Debug build/ tree price at 0 CE total 73130 ms with era-1 26189 ms, and 1960 two-span total 57792 ms with era-1 13838 ms. The era pass is 3.9% of a Release build and 36% of a Debug one - a ~9x difference in SHARE - so the derived ratio "the era costs 4x its own wall clock" is a Release fact and reads 1.45x in Debug. What reproduces across BOTH build types, and is the finding that matters, is the DIRECTION: the two-span 1960 world builds FASTER than the single-span 0 CE one (57.8 s vs 73.1 s in Debug, 8.0 s vs 8.2 s in Release). Quote no ratio from this row without its build type.

rows.evidence: COMPLETE 2026-09-06. src/world/landscape_score.{hpp,cpp}. Term 1 delegates to BL-775 promoted measure_market_completeness (two callers, one implementation). Term 2 is the per-market per-resource supply:demand ratio with a pin band. Term 3 is the coefficient of variation over markets - CV rather than variance deliberately, because it is scale-free, so a landscape uniformly twice as good scores as MORE VIABLE and no more UNEVEN. Unevenness is a MULTIPLIER on viability, never an addend: a landscape where nothing works is not rescued by being unevenly broken. Recipe margin correctly excluded.

rows.requirement: THE SLICE'S ACTUAL QUESTION: scoring several hand-made candidate landscapes on one generated world produces MATERIALLY DIFFERENT scores. If the terms do not discriminate, that is the reported result and the search is not built.

rows.notes: The slice is built to be able to FAIL. A flat completeness across every candidate means the search has nothing to search on, and that answer is the deliverable.
rows.evidence:
COMPLETE 2026-09-06 - AND THE ANSWER IS NO. Five candidates on one fixed world (corporation_count 4/8/16, two placement seeds at 8 - exactly Ben point-3 axes) score IDENTICALLY to the last digit: every term relative range 0.000e+00. The POSITIVE CONTROL, built in so that "flat" could be told from "constant", moves 1.000e+00 over three different worlds. CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL: every term reads tiles, markets and population, and market_saturation.cpp contains neither "corporation" nor "building" - so the objective measures the WORLD saturation potential, not a roster realisation of it. Phase 6 cannot search on it as ruled. A roster-aware term (actual vs potential completeness) is owed; recorded on BL-770, deliberately not built in this slice.

CORRECTED 2026-09-06 AFTER THE COLD REVIEW BARRIER. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVED, AND IS NOW PROPERLY CONTROLLED. The review found the negative result had no FIXTURE control: "flat across candidates" was indistinguishable from "the candidates never differed". Added R2.0, which asserts the fixtures move before any conclusion is drawn. MEASURED: corps 149..169 and buildings 415..456 across the five candidates - they differ materially - and every score term is still bit-identical at 0.000e+00. The finding is stronger than when first reported. ONE CLAIM WITHDRAWN: section B's three 1.000e+00 readings are largely an ARTEFACT. relative_range is (hi-lo)/hi and seed ABCDEF01 generates a ONE-MARKET world, whose spread is definitionally 0 and whose composite is therefore 0 - so those terms read 1.000 by dividing against a zero floor. Only chain completeness (3.432e-01) is real control signal. That is enough to carry the conclusion, but the control is weaker than first stated.

rows.requirement: The scorer is PURE and deterministic: same world and same candidate produce the same score, and the score does not depend on container traversal order.
verification: headless: the market walk uses sorted_market_ids, not world::markets order
rows.notes: Determinism is the binding constraint on the eventual parallel search - it is asserted from the first slice, not retrofitted.
rows.evidence:
COMPLETE 2026-09-06. R3.1 asserts three scorings of one world are bit-identical on every term - PASS. The market walk uses sorted_market_ids. NOTED IN THE SOURCE rather than hidden: the tile accumulation is float += over the unordered w.tiles map, which is sound for RANKING candidates within one process (every candidate sees the identical traversal) and would need a sorted walk before any cross-process comparison. Submitted to the cold review barrier specifically to be attacked on this point.

CORRECTED 2026-09-06 AFTER THE COLD REVIEW BARRIER. R3 WAS MARKED COMPLETE ON EVIDENCE THAT DID NOT BEAR ON THE CLAIM, and this was the review's most serious finding. The scorer summed DOUBLES over w.tiles, an unordered_map - making the result depend on hash bucket layout, which varies by standard library. src/world/CLAUDE.md forbids exactly this with no "same process" carve-out, and market_saturation.cpp - the sibling this file delegates term 1 to - REFUSES the same thing in a comment at its own tile walk. The first cut wrote a rationalisation instead of following the local invariant. And R3.1 could never have caught it: it scores the SAME world object three times, so it shares one bucket layout by construction. FIXED: the tile walk is now sorted by entity_id before accumulation. The amplification made it worse than theoretical - the entire term-2 signal on the default world is ONE resource in ONE of three markets, so a single ULP flip would have taken composite from 0.0099 to 0.

rows.requirement: The pre-game warm start runs BEFORE the player is seated, under corp_ai_params::spectating, with no corp flagged is_player for its whole duration.
The shortlist is the specialists clearing the viability floor; the seat is drawn from it against the WORLD SEED, so one seed reproduces one seat exactly across runs.

The draw is WEIGHTED, not uniform (Ben, 2026-08-26): a processor among the holdings weights up, and holdings on or near populated ground weight up. It is a BIAS, never a gate - a pure-extraction corp on thin ground stays drawable. The resulting distribution is REPORTED across a sweep, never asserted against a target.
An unmet floor STANDS: if no specialist clears, the highest trailing-net specialist is seated and the world records that the floor went unmet. No corp is conjured or patched.
